facts.statement: The first fossil of Anthracosuchus was discovered in the Cerrejón mine in La Guajira, Colombia, in 2005.
facts.quote: The first fossil of Anthracosuchus was found in the Cerrejón mine in La Guajira, Colombia, in 2005.

facts.statement: The species name 'balrogus' honors the Balrog from J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, a creature known for dwelling in mines like the fossil remains.
facts.quote: The species name is a reference to the Balrog, a creature in J. R. R. Tolkien's fantasy novel The Lord of the Rings that could, like the remains of Anthracosuchus, be found in a mine.

facts.statement: The only known species, Anthracosuchus balrogus, is represented by four fossil specimens with partial skulls found in the Cerrejón Formation.
facts.quote: Remains of Anthracosuchus balrogus, the only known species, come from the Cerrejón Formation in the Cerrejón mine, and include four fossil specimens with partial skulls.

facts.statement: Anthracosuchus possesses five osteoderms with a thick cross-section and unpitted surfaces, contrasting with the flat, pitted osteoderms of typical dyrosaurids.
facts.quote: There are 5 osteoderms associated with Anthracosuchus, all of which possess a thick cross section and an unpitted ventral and dorsal surface, while those of more typical dyrosaurids such as Hyposaurus are flat with wide pits.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Anthracosuchus may have practiced subsurface predation, differing from the feeding methods of other dyrosaurs.
facts.quote: This could present a deviation of feeding method in Anthracosuchus from other dyrosaurs, possibly subsurface predation.

facts.statement: The robust, broad, and low-crowned teeth of Anthracosuchus suggest a durophagous diet involving a crushing bite on hard-shelled prey.
facts.quote: The teeth of Anthracosuchus are broad, blunt and low crowned. This robust dentition may indicate a durophagous diet, preying on hard-shelled prey using a crushing bite.

facts.statement: The vertical muscle attachment on Anthracosuchus ribs suggests it swam with a more undulating motion than modern crocodylians.
facts.quote: Anthracosuchus ribs indicate a vertical attachment of the muscles, allowing for a more undulating way of swimming when compared to extant crocodylians, further aided less extensive lateral osteoderm density.

facts.statement: Because its osteoderms do not overlap, Anthracosuchus likely had greater flexibility than other dyrosaurs but reduced stability.
facts.quote: Anthracosuchus, whose osteoderms do not imbricate at all, may have had an even greater degree of flexibility compared to other dyrosaurs, at the cost of reduced stability.

facts.statement: Anthracosuchus is classified as one of the most basal dyrosaurids, alongside Chenanisuchus and Cerrejonisuchus.
facts.quote: It is one of the most basal dyrosaurids along with Chenanisuchus and Cerrejonisuchus.

facts.statement: Anthracosuchus lived during the Mid-Late Paleocene epoch.
The time range for Anthracosuchus is estimated from 61.66 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Thanetian (61.66 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Anthracosuchus balrogus are found in the Cerrejón Formation within the Cerrejón mine.
facts.quote: Remains of Anthracosuchus balrogus, the only known species, come from the Cerrejón Formation in the Cerrejón mine

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (UF/IGM 67) includes a nearly complete, dorsoventrally compressed skull, nine ribs, seven vertebrae, and unidentified bones.
facts.quote: The holotype of Anthracosuchus (UF/IGM 67) consists of a nearly complete, dorsoventrally compressed skull, 9 ribs, 7 vertebrae and unidentified bones.

facts.statement: The paratype (UF/IGM 68) contains a nearly complete uncompressed skull (missing the premaxilla tip and right articular), three teeth, and postcranial elements including five osteoderms, five vertebrae, eight ribs, and parts of the pelvis.
facts.quote: The paratype (UF/IGM 68) includes a nearly complete skull in an uncompressed state, however missing the anterior most tip of the premaxilla, the right articular, 3 associated teeth as well as various parts of the postcranial skeleton such as 5 osteoderms, 5 vertebrae, 8 ribs, the distal parts of the pubis and ischium, a haemal arch, a sacral rib as well as a proximal phalanx and several unidentified bones.

rejected.statement: Three additional specimens were discovered in 2007, following the initial find in 2005.
rejected.quote: The second specimen followed in early 2007 with two more being discovered later that same year.
